# Kigumi CLI - Web Awesome Component Library for React

Kigumi provides a CLI tool to add Web Awesome components to React projects with framework-specific wrappers.

## Quick Start

```bash
npx kigumi init        # Initialize project
npx kigumi add button  # Add components
```

## Components

57+ components available across categories:
- **Actions**: Button, ButtonGroup, CopyButton, Dropdown, QrCode
- **Form Controls**: Input, Checkbox, Radio, RadioGroup, Select, Slider, Switch, Textarea
- **Navigation**: Breadcrumb, Tab, TabGroup, Tree
- **Organization**: Card, Dialog, Drawer, Details, Divider
- **Feedback**: Badge, Callout, ProgressBar, Spinner, Tag, Tooltip
- **Imagery**: Avatar, Carousel, Icon, AnimatedImage
- **Utilities**: Animation, FormatDate, FormatNumber, Popup, Popover

**Full list**: `npx kigumi list`

## AI Agent Skills

For AI-assisted transformation of Web Awesome HTML to Kigumi components:

### Install the Skill

```bash
# Via skills CLI
npx skills add https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Siregar/kigumi-cli/main/skills/transform-webawesome-to-react

# Or manually from installed package
npm install kigumi
cp -r ./node_modules/kigumi/dist/skills/transform-webawesome-to-react .cursor/skills/
```

### How It Works

1. Paste Web Awesome HTML to your AI assistant
2. Ask: "Convert this to Kigumi React"
3. Get transformed code with proper imports
4. Detects missing components and suggests installation commands

**Example**:

Input (Web Awesome):
```html
<wa-card>
  <wa-button variant="brand">Click me</wa-button>
</wa-card>
```

Output (Kigumi React):
```tsx
import { Button, Card } from '@/components/ui';

<Card>
  <Button variant="brand">Click me</Button>
</Card>
```

### Available Skills

- **transform-webawesome-to-react**: Transform Web Awesome HTML to React components

Full documentation: [skills/README.md](https://github.com/Siregar/kigumi-cli/blob/main/skills/README.md)
